| [THEORY-030](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-030.md) v3 | For a memory evolving reversibly with its environment, Landauer's bound prices only steps that lose logical distinguishability, at least k ln 2 of entropy per bit lost, exported to the environment and not necessarily as heat, so copying onto a blank register, measuring or evaluating a bit has no minimum cost; learning a label has a floor only in total entropy production, at least the information learnt, which in Goldt and Seifert's perceptron can be paid in the weights' own entropy with vanishing heat | Bennett (2003), [LIT-360](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-360.md): the cost attaches to many-to-one maps of the logical state, at least k ln 2 of entropy per bit exported to non-information-bearing degrees of freedom, which "need not" be heat. Goldt & Seifert ([LIT-308](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-308.md)) bound information learnt by total entropy production, payable with vanishing heat in their toy model. It does not license a k_BT ln 2 heat floor per judgment, per gradient step or per bit learnt. | [THEORY-568](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-568.md) | Whatever redundancy measure a partial information decomposition uses, provided its atoms satisfy the consistency equation, the average number of single sources an atom can be read from is Σᵢ I(Xᵢ;Y)/I(X;Y) and the average number of sources it cannot do without is Σⱼ I(Xⱼ;Y\|X₋ⱼ)/I(X;Y); so the redundancy–synergy index equals (r̄ − 1)·I(X;Y), and for three or more sources it counts a k-way redundancy k − 1 times but synergy once | Gutknecht et al. (2025), [LIT-042](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-042.md), read in full in [NOTE-045](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-045.md), with the combinatorial proofs of Props. 1–4 and 6 checked by hand. The averages need only the consistency equation and I(X;Y) > 0; reading them as average degrees, and the bounds of Appendix B, need non-negative atoms. Corollary 5 overstates Prop. 6 (⇔ for ⇐). The network results are on tiny quantised models evaluated on their own training sets, and are not part of this account. | Active |
| [THEORY-581](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-581.md) v2 | Two exactly consistent descriptions of one system, at different scales and with equal past–future mutual information, can differ in how that information divides between redundancy and synergy; in small generated Boolean networks under the Williams–Beer redundancy measure the coarser scale was more synergy-biased in every random stochastic system, by at most about 0.07, and the direction mostly reversed for redundancy-biased deterministic ones | Varley & Hoel (2022), [LIT-027](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-027.md), read in [NOTE-020](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-020.md). Expanding a 3-node macroscale TPM into 4- and 5-node equivalence-class microscales holds mutual information fixed with zero inconsistency, so any change in the PID's synergy bias B_syn is a change of type, not of amount. In 200 \|Gaussian\| TPMs the macroscale gained B_syn by about 0.005–0.07; in 185 near-deterministic ones most with macro B_syn < 0.5 lost it. One redundancy function, no robustness check, tiny constructed systems. The "unifying theory" of the title is a framing: the EI section re-describes a known decomposition and adds no result. | Active |
| [THEORY-584](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-584.md) | The quantum fidelity tr√(ρ1^{1/2}ρ0ρ1^{1/2}) is exactly the classical Bhattacharyya overlap of the two states' outcome distributions minimized over all measurements, and the minimum is attained by a projective measurement whose eigenvalues are square roots of likelihood ratios | Fuchs (1995), [LIT-018](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-018.md), read in full in [NOTE-021](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-021.md). min over POVMs of Σ_b √(tr ρ0E_b)√(tr ρ1E_b) equals tr√(ρ1^{1/2}ρ0ρ1^{1/2}) (Eq. 3.28), attained in the eigenbasis of M = ρ1^{-1/2}√(ρ1^{1/2}ρ0ρ1^{1/2})ρ1^{-1/2} (Eq. 3.67), whose eigenvalues are √(tr ρ0E_b / tr ρ1E_b) (Eq. 3.92). Proved for invertible ρ1 with a separate support construction, in finite dimension. The fidelity is the unsquared one; Jozsa's is its square. The thesis says nothing about trace distance, and the analogous problems for Rényi overlaps and the quantum Chernoff bound are left open. | Active |
| [THEORY-599](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-599.md) | In trained neural-network weights stored as BF16 or FP32, nearly all the redundancy a lossless coder can remove lies in the floating-point exponent, which occupies about 40 of its 256 values and compresses to about a third under single-symbol Huffman coding, while sign and mantissa are near-incompressible; the redundancy belongs to the number format, not to the learned function | Hershcovitch et al. (2024), ZipNN, [LIT-268](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-268.md), read in full in [NOTE-241](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-241.md). Fifteen models broken down by byte group (Table II), with the exponent skew shown on four (Fig. 2) from 1 GB middle slices. A parameter shuffle changes Zstd's exponent compression by at most 0.05%, so the gain is order-0. The paper never computes an entropy. Its explanation of the skew is partly wrong as stated, and its remark that the redundancy shows overparametrization unused does not follow from what it measured. | Active |
| [THEORY-602](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-602.md) | An ergodic source's entropy is the least average rate at which it can be encoded, a noisy channel has a capacity below which any rate can be sent with arbitrarily small error and above which the equivocation cannot fall below the excess, and a source can be reproduced at a given fidelity over a channel exactly when its rate for that fidelity does not exceed the capacity; Shannon rests the justification of entropy on these theorems, not on the axioms that single out −Σ p log p | Shannon (1948), [LIT-764](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-764.md), read in [NOTE-591](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-591.md): Parts I–II closely, Parts III–V and the later appendices skimmed for their theorem statements. The noisy-channel achievability proof is a random-coding sketch at the typical-set level, not a full ε–δ argument, and the strong converse is not proved; the theorems themselves were later made rigorous. Shannon says the uniqueness theorem for H is "in no way necessary" to the theory. The theorems assume ergodic, finite-state sources and channels and say nothing about meaning. | Active |
| [THEORY-617](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-617.md) | In additive Gaussian noise independent of an input of finite power whose law does not depend on the signal-to-noise ratio, the derivative of mutual information with respect to that ratio is half the minimum mean-square error of the optimal noncausal estimator, so mutual information is accumulated estimation error over SNR; in continuous time the causal filtering error equals the noncausal error averaged over SNR, and the identity fails with feedback | Guo, Shamai & Verdú (2004), [LIT-058](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-058.md), read in full in [NOTE-086](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-086.md). Proved five ways for every finite-power input, in scalar, vector, discrete-time and continuous-time forms. It concerns the optimal, conditional-mean estimator; carrying it to a trained diffusion model's learned denoiser needs the mismatched version, which is later work. Theorems 3, 4 and 11 are stated without proof. | Active |
| [THEORY-641](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-641.md) v2 | Under a well-specified, identifiable parametric Markov model of the target given the joint past, with ergodic lagged states, transfer entropy is the limit of the normalised log-likelihood ratio for the null of no dependence on the source's past, so it is Granger-sense predictive improvement; for finite-state chains the plug-in estimator is exactly that statistic, and under the null and the usual regularity it is asymptotically χ² with the difference in parameter counts as degrees of freedom | Barnett & Bossomaier (2012), [LIT-048](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-048.md), read in full in [NOTE-053](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-053.md). The consistency result is a one-line consequence of Props. 1–2, and Prop. 2 is argued informally. The χ² null is imported from Wald (1943), whose regularity conditions are not checked. The non-central χ² for T > 0 is at best a local-alternative approximation. The finite-state identity and the Gaussian equivalence (half the Granger statistic) are exact. | Active |
| [THEORY-668](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-668.md) | When the encoder is restricted to prunings of one fixed hierarchy of nested partitions, any non-negatively weighted sum of relevant information, irrelevant information and compression decomposes into per-node terms, so a bottom-up recursion finds the unique optimal tree with fewest leaves exactly in linear time, while greedy top-down splitting can miss information lying below a level that carries none; penalising irrelevant information only prunes the information-bottleneck tree | Larsson, Maity & Tsiotras (2022), [LIT-868](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-868.md), read in full in [NOTE-676](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-676.md), every proof followed step by step. The decomposition is the chain rule for refinements, and the recursion is the classic bottom-up pruning of a fixed tree. [NOTE-676](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-676.md) declined a THEORY as exact but narrow; it is filed because the reading supports it as stated and its greedy-failure point bears on how hierarchy is measured. The hierarchy is given, not found, and the evaluation is one image. | Active |
| [THEORY-676](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-676.md) | Dewar's information-theoretic derivation of maximum entropy production does not reach the far-from-equilibrium regime where the principle is applied: the 2003 route needs a mean-field step and an unargued assumption about path counts, the 2005 route's orthogonality condition, which yields both maximum and minimum dissipation, holds only with linear constitutive relations, and the 2003 self-organized-criticality corollary is an artefact of a quadratic expansion | Grinstein & Linsker (2007), [LIT-525](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-525.md), read in [NOTE-422](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-422.md), against Dewar (2003), [LIT-521](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-521.md), read in [NOTE-426](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-426.md). The self-organized-criticality point was checked against Dewar 2003 and is correct. The linearity point concerns Dewar 2005, which the record could not read; it is held on the Comment's account of its equations and on an exactly solvable spin chain, re-derived. The Comment removes one derivation and one application. It does not say MEP is false, and it says the existence of far-from-equilibrium extremal principles "has not been settled". | Active |
| [THEORY-695](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-695.md) | Two quantum states can be broadcast if and only if they commute, and cloned if and only if they are identical or orthogonal; the theorem is proved for invertible density operators and marks a line within quantum theory, not a witness of nonclassicality | Fuchs (1995), [LIT-018](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-018.md), §4.3, read in full in [NOTE-021](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-021.md), from the Barnum–Caves–Fuchs–Jozsa–Schumacher manuscript. Fidelity cannot decrease under partial trace or under the broadcasting map, so broadcasting forces equality conditions that make ρ0 commute with the optimal-fidelity operator. Proved for invertible ρ0, ρ1 only. Spekkens' epistricted classical theories ([LIT-007](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-007.md)) reproduce no-broadcasting, so the theorem states where broadcastability ends inside quantum theory and does not by itself certify nonclassicality. | Active |
| [THEORY-700](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-700.md) | For jointly Gaussian stationary processes, Granger causality in Geweke's generalized-variance form is exactly twice the transfer entropy, conditional and multivariate, at the regressions' lags, because least-squares residual covariance is the partial covariance and a Gaussian's conditional entropy is half its log-determinant plus a constant | Barnett, Barrett & Seth (2009), [LIT-1171](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1171.md), read in full in [NOTE-934](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-934.md). F_{Y→X\|Z} = 2T_{Y→X\|Z}, exactly, for population quantities. The proof is two identities and was checked. Sample agreement depends on the entropy estimator. Both quantities are predictive; the authors keep them apart from physical causation. | Active |
| [THEORY-701](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-701.md) | Transfer entropy from J to I is the Kullback entropy of assuming that I's next state, given its last k states, does not depend on J's last l states, so it is zero exactly when J's past leaves I's transition law unchanged; unlike time-delayed mutual information it is directional and zero for static correlation, and it removes a common input only when that input is conditioned on | Schreiber (2000), [LIT-1177](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1177.md), read in full in [NOTE-940](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-940.md). The definition and its zero condition are exact. The comparison with delayed mutual information rests on two coupled-map lattices built with a known direction. The continuum-limit claim is asserted. The Letter's tent-map coefficient appears to be twice what Eq. 4 gives. | Active |
| [THEORY-702](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-702.md) | Transfer entropy is the average of a local transfer entropy, the log ratio at each observation of the destination's next-state probability with and without the source given the destination's past, which can be negative where the source misleads; the destination history must be long for it to exclude self-influence routed through the source; and conditioning also on the destination's other causal parents (complete) can differ sharply from conditioning on its past alone (apparent), as in elementary cellular automata, where long-history local transfer entropy picks out gliders and domain walls | Lizier, Prokopenko & Zomaya (2008), [LIT-1175](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1175.md), read in full in [NOTE-943](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-943.md). The local decomposition is an identity; the claims about k and about particles rest on elementary CAs judged by eye. Three worked local values and rule 18's XOR structure were checked. | Active |
| [THEORY-705](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-705.md) v2 | For a target and two sources with finite alphabets, if unique information is to depend only on the two source–target pair marginals, then the minimum of the conditional mutual information over all joints with those marginals is an upper bound on every non-negative decomposition's unique information, and the shared and synergistic information it implies are lower bounds; this unique information vanishes exactly when the other source is Blackwell-sufficient, and the measures are non-negative, satisfy the bivariate partial-information axioms and the identity property, and do not extend to three sources on the partial-information lattice | Bertschinger et al. (2014), [LIT-1162](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1162.md), read in full in [NOTE-937](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-937.md). The bounds, the Blackwell characterisation and the properties are proved. The motivating property is argued, not derived. Example 30 and the Table 1 rows reproduce, except two entries that conflict with the paper's own Proposition 18. Under this measure, the record's transfer-entropy examples split exactly as under I_min. | Active |
| [THEORY-706](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-706.md) | Any redundancy function defined on the lattice of antichains of sources, ordered so that a collection precedes another when every source of the latter contains one of the former, has a Möbius inverse that decomposes the information a set of sources gives about a target into partial-information atoms summing to every subset's mutual information; for the I_min redundancy, the expected minimum specific information over sources, every atom is nonnegative, and interaction information is a signed mixture of atoms, synergy minus redundancy for three variables | Williams & Beer (2010), [LIT-1172](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1172.md), read in full in [NOTE-936](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-936.md). The lattice, the inversion and the nonnegativity proofs are exact and were followed; the lattice sizes and the 3-parity and three-copies cases were checked. What is not shown is that I_min measures shared information: it gives two independent copied bits 1 bit of redundancy (Harder, Salge and Polani). | Active |
| [THEORY-707](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-707.md) | Transfer entropy is not a measure of information flow, if flow means information in the target attributable solely to the source's past: as a conditional mutual information it equals the source's unique information plus its synergy with the target's past, so it can credit a full bit to a source that carries none alone (Y_t = X_{t−1} ⊕ Y_{t−1}) and report zero from each of two sources that jointly fix the target (Z_t = X_{t−1} ⊕ Y_{t−1}); conditioning on further series, as causation entropy does, has the same fault | James, Barnett & Crutchfield (2016), [LIT-1165](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1165.md), read in full in [NOTE-945](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-945.md). Both examples are exact and were recomputed. The decomposition holds for any PID satisfying the consistency equations. The conclusion is relative to the authors' definition of flow; transfer entropy as predictive improvement is untouched. The claims about directed information, interventional flow and Gaussian systems are cited or conjectured. | Active |
| [THEORY-708](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-708.md) v2 | The I_min redundancy credits two independent sources with shared information whenever each reduces surprise about the same target outcomes, so it gives two independent bits copied into the target 1 bit of redundancy; a bivariate redundancy built from reverse information projections, each source's information less what is lost when its posteriors are replaced by mixtures of the other's, satisfies symmetry, self-redundancy, monotonicity and the identity property, gives a nonnegative decomposition, and agrees with I_min on XOR, AND and their compositions but can reverse the state-independent/state-dependent split of a transfer entropy | Harder, Salge & Polani (2013), [LIT-1168](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1168.md), read in full in [NOTE-944](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-944.md). The counterexample, the axioms and the nonnegativity proof are exact; every Table I value and both transfer-entropy examples were recomputed. The identity axiom and "mechanistic redundancy" are positions, not results, and the measure is bivariate only. | Active |
| [THEORY-709](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-709.md) | Mutual information between continuous variables can be estimated from k-nearest-neighbour statistics, with the joint k-th-neighbour distance in the maximum norm fixing the scale at which marginal neighbours are counted, so that the biases of the three entropy estimates largely cancel; the one approximation is a locally constant density, the systematic error scales with k/N, and exactness for independent variables is observed in every tested case but not proved | Kraskov, Stögbauer & Grassberger (2004), [LIT-1163](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1163.md), read in [NOTE-938](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-938.md) (formal sections in full, numerics at lower resolution). The estimators are derived up to one approximation and one neglected correction; the rest is numerical. Checked by simulation on correlated Gaussians. | Active |
| [THEORY-710](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-710.md) | In a finite causal Bayesian network, a set of nodes is causally independent of another, imposing a third, for every choice of mechanisms exactly when every directed path between them passes through the third; information flow, conditional mutual information computed from interventional instead of observational distributions, vanishes under causal independence, and it can differ from transfer entropy and conditional mutual information in either direction | Ay & Polani (2008), [LIT-1174](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1174.md), read in full in [NOTE-946](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-946.md) from the 2006 preprint. Theorem 2 and Prop. 3 are proved; Examples 3–6 were recomputed. Example 6's one bit holds at k = 1 and fails for k ≥ 2 as stated. The measure needs the mechanisms, and estimation and identification are not addressed. | Active |
| [THEORY-711](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-711.md) | Directed information from an input sequence to an output sequence, the sum over time of the information the inputs up to now carry about the current output given the past outputs, is at most their mutual information and equal to it when the channel is used without feedback; in a causal system it bounds what the output reveals about the source, so feedback cannot raise a memoryless channel's capacity; and the usual definition of a memoryless channel holds only without feedback | Massey (1990), [LIT-1166](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1166.md), read in full in [NOTE-939](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-939.md) from the author's preprint. Three short theorems, all checked; the feedback inequality also checked numerically. "Causal" is Massey's factorization condition, not intervention. That directed information is full-history transfer entropy plus instantaneous terms is the record's derivation. | Active |
| [THEORY-712](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-712.md) v2 | Under any partial information decomposition satisfying the consistency equations, a transfer entropy T_{Y→X} = I(X_{t+1}; Y_t \| X_t) is the unique information of the source's past about the target's next state plus the synergy of source and target pasts, which Williams and Beer call state-independent and state-dependent transfer; time-delayed mutual information is the unique part plus redundancy; with the I_min redundancy the state-independent part alone suffices for perfect open-loop control, and a two-source transfer entropy splits into unique, redundant and synergistic transfer | Williams & Beer (2011), [LIT-1176](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1176.md), an arXiv preprint, read in full in [NOTE-942](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-942.md). The two-term split is an identity from the consistency equations; the sizes of the terms, the control theorem and the multivariate split use I_min, which the record has not read argued for. The one-parameter family and the three corners of the two-source family were recomputed. The text mislabels the synergistic corner. | Active |
| [THEORY-713](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-713.md) | No redundancy measure on the Williams–Beer partial-information lattice can satisfy symmetry, self-redundancy, monotonicity, the identity axiom and non-negative atoms once there are three sources: for two independent bits, their XOR and a target that copies all three, identity forces three one-bit atoms under a two-bit total, so one atom is at most −1 bit, and a multivariate decomposition that keeps identity must give up non-negativity or the lattice | Rauh, Bertschinger, Olbrich & Jost (2014), [LIT-1202](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1202.md), read in full in [NOTE-965](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-965.md). A proved impossibility, checked by hand and by script. It also uses invariance of redundancy under relabelling the target, which is not stated as an axiom. I_min escapes it by failing identity, Ince's I_ccs by accepting the −1-bit atom. | Active |
| [THEORY-714](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-714.md) v3 | Ince's I_ccs, the expected local co-information over only those events where every source, the joint source and the overlap change the target's surprisal in the same direction, under the maximum-entropy joint that preserves the source–target and joint-source marginals, is symmetric and self-redundant and satisfies the independent identity property; it fails Harder et al.'s identity and monotonicity, so its atoms can be negative, and, though its paper says otherwise, it fails subset equality | Ince (2017), [LIT-1201](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1201.md), read in [NOTE-968](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-968.md). The definition is exact, and three of the four properties the paper claims hold; subset equality does not (re-derived 2026-10-20), and every discrete example reproduces. That the dropped properties ought to be dropped, and that unique information depends on the source–source marginal, are argued, not proved. Whether it is the right redundancy measure is open (QUESTION-223). It meets Rauh et al.'s −1-bit bound exactly on XORCOPY. | Active |
| [THEORY-715](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-715.md) | The information about a target carried by the Gács–Körner common random variable of the sources is a redundancy defined for any number of sources that is nonnegative, target-monotone and no larger than I_min, and is a lower bound on any reasonable redundancy; but it counts only deterministic shared structure, so it is zero whenever the sources' joint distribution has full support, fails the identity property and continuity, and gives negative synergy already for two sources | Griffith, Chong, James, Ellison & Crutchfield (2014), [LIT-1203](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1203.md), read in full in [NOTE-967](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-967.md). The lemmas are short and exact, and every example was recomputed, with Harder, Salge and Polani's copy family and a three-source copy added. It is the record's one redundancy defined for n > 2, and it does not have the identity property there or for n = 2. | Active |
| [THEORY-716](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-716.md) | Synergy can be measured as the whole minus the union of its parts, the union information being the least information the sources could jointly carry about the target with every source–target marginal held fixed; this synergy lies between WholeMinusSum and Williams and Beer's S_max, which respectively subtract redundancy and count unique information as synergy, and for two sources it is Bertschinger et al.'s synergy, so independent sources can share information about a target, as the authors' last version concedes against their first | Griffith & Koch (2014), [LIT-1204](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1204.md), read in full in [NOTE-966](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-966.md), v6 with v1–v2 checked. The definitions, the criticisms of S_max, WMS and ΔI, and the properties proved in Appendix C are exact, and every Table 1 value for two predictors was recomputed. The identification with Bertschinger et al.'s CI for two sources is the record's derivation. Monotonicity is claimed without proof, and the S_max bound's proof has a step the reading could not reconstruct. | Active |
| [THEORY-717](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-717.md) | For experiments with finitely many states and finitely many outcomes, being at least as informative in every decision problem is the same as being reproducible from the other by a Markov matrix | Blackwell (1953), [LIT-781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-781.md), Theorems 4–6, read in [NOTE-595](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-595.md): the Sherman– Stein theorem, with a new minimax proof. With n states and finite outcome sets, write experiments as n × N Markov matrices P and Q. Every risk vector Q attains in every decision problem is attainable with P exactly when Q = PM for some Markov matrix M. The arbitrary-outcome extension is [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md), still Proposed. A qualitative order: most pairs are incomparable, and it says nothing about how far apart they are. | Active |
| [THEORY-719](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-719.md) | On a finite augmentation space, over unconstrained functions of the two views, the spectral contrastive and NT-Logistic losses are both minimized at the positive-pair density ratio | Johnson, El Hanchi & Maddison (2023), [LIT-258](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-258.md), App. B.2–B.3, read in [NOTE-751](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-751.md): on a finite augmentation space, with every function of the two views allowed, the spectral contrastive loss is minimized by K⁺ = p⁺/(p⊗p) exactly, and the NT-Logistic loss with equal positive and negative classes by the log-odds log K⁺, so its exponentiated score is K⁺. Population optima over unconstrained functions only; not what an encoder reaches, and not InfoNCE, which is [THEORY-001](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-001.md)'s open part. | Active |
| [THEORY-733](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-733.md) | For a stable linear Gaussian VAR(p), a linear coarse-graining is exactly dynamically independent iff its row space is invariant under the transpose of every lag matrix, so for p ≥ 2 almost no parameter set has one at any scale, while for p = 1 they are the transpose's invariant subspaces, which exist on open sets but not generically at every scale | Barnett and Seth (2023), [LIT-979](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-979.md), read in [NOTE-791](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-791.md): the VAR form (3.26) of exact dynamical independence, with the genericity count of §3.3 made a proof for VAR order p ≥ 2 and corrected for p = 1. Linear coarse-grainings Y = LX of a stable VAR with non-degenerate Gaussian innovations only. It says nothing about near-independence, about the multimodality of the dynamical-dependence cost, or about nonlinear maps. | Active |
| [THEORY-742](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-742.md) v2 | For a Boltzmann distribution linear in its couplings, observed through any coarse-graining map, the Fisher information the coarse data lose about the bare couplings is the expected conditional covariance of the energy operators given the coarse state; when the renormalized Hamiltonian stays in the family, the parameter map is linear and the additive constant of the step is analytic, that loss is the constant's Hessian, so the singular part of the metric passes unchanged to the coarse data. In the hopping model of diffusion at its Gaussian fixed point, keeping every n-th position of a trajectory of fixed duration multiplies the metric by n^(1−μ) in the μ-th Hermite coordinate: the drift's information is kept exactly, the variance's falls as 1/n, and higher shape parameters' faster | Raju, Machta and Sethna (2018), [LIT-1254](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1254.md), read in [NOTE-972](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-972.md). The loss identity holds for any coarse-graining of an exponential family; that the loss is analytic, and so spares the singular part of the metric, needs an exact renormalization step with linear beta functions and an analytic constant. It does not say that relevant directions keep their information in general: on the paper's own scalings only directions with RG eigenvalue above d/2 do, and away from the Gaussian fixed point even the drift loses information. | Active |
| [THEORY-743](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-743.md) | For finite X and Y, every information-bottleneck optimum at every β gives one encoder to all inputs sharing p(y\|x), so it is a stochastic coarsening of the minimal sufficient partition (the causal states of memoryless transduction); as β → ∞ the optima converge to that partition, but in general no finite β attains it, except when Y is a function of X | Shalizi and Crutchfield ([LIT-1240](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1240.md), read in [NOTE-976](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-976.md)) assert that the information bottleneck recovers the causal states as β → ∞. The record proves it, against stochastic encoders as well as partitions, and adds that every finite-β optimum factors through those states. So the IB hierarchy always nests under its top. It says nothing about whether optima at two finite β nest. Finite alphabets only. | Active |
| [THEORY-748](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-748.md) | Block entropies, and so every lag-τ entropy rate of a stationary signal, are unchanged by the reflection x → −x and by time reversal, so they cannot detect the odd-order asymmetry the 4/5 law ties to energy flux; Granero-Belinchón, Roux and Garnier's entropy rate conditioned on the sign of the increment breaks the reflection invariance, but h⁺ ≠ h⁻ shows only that the two-point distribution lacks central symmetry, which a skewed one-point distribution produces with exactly symmetric increments, so the test does not by itself detect skewed increments or an energy cascade | Granero-Belinchón, Roux and Garnier (2016), [LIT-1243](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1243.md), read in [NOTE-970](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-970.md), claim that conditioning the entropy rate on the sign of the increment lets one "prove the existence of the energy cascade" using information theory. The record finds two limits. The unconditioned entropy rate is exactly blind to reflection and time reversal. The conditioned one detects any central asymmetry of the two-point law, including one with no increment skewness at all. Independent pairs with the paper's one-point skewness of 0.175 give h⁺ − h⁻ ≈ 0.066 nats with symmetric increments. Nothing in the paper ties an information quantity to the energy balance. | Active |
| [THEORY-750](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-750.md) | For a stationary Gaussian signal the lag-τ entropy rate with one-point embedding is h_τ = H(X) + ½ log(1 − c(τ)²), so where the normalized second-order structure function 1 − c(τ) is small and scales as τ^ζ₂, h_τ = (ζ₂/2) log τ + constant; the "scaling of information" that Granero-Belinchón, Roux and Garnier measure in near-Gaussian wind-tunnel turbulence, slope 1/3 in the inertial range and 1 in the dissipative range, is the scaling of the second-order structure function written in nats | Granero-Belinchón, Roux and Garnier (2016), [LIT-1243](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1243.md), read in full in [NOTE-970](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-970.md). A Gaussian identity and its small-lag asymptotics: the conditional entropy of x(t) given x(t − τ) is a monotone function of the autocorrelation, so its scaling exponent is half the structure-function exponent. In the Modane data the estimated entropy rate matches the Gaussian formula, so the measured "information spectrum" is S₂ again. It is not a distribution of a conserved quantity over scales, and it carries nothing about the direction or size of energy transfer. It answers [QUESTION-219](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-219.md) only in the narrow sense of supporting A3's caution. | Active |
| [THEORY-751](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-751.md) v2 | For a memoryless source with finite alphabets and a per-letter distortion, a description at rate R(D₁) can be refined to distortion D₂ < D₁ at total rate R(D₂) iff some pair of rate–distortion-optimal test channels forms a Markov chain X → X̂₂ → X̂₁; the condition holds for every discrete source under Hamming distortion and fails for some three-letter sources under absolute error | Equitz and Cover (1991), [LIT-1238](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1238.md), read in [NOTE-988](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-988.md), with every step re-derived by 2026-10-20. Lossless two-stage description is possible exactly when the coarse optimum is a stochastic degradation of the fine optimum. That is a Markov chain on test channels, not nesting of partitions, and it is an asymptotic block-coding statement. It does not say that optimal single-shot quantizers or deterministic encoders nest, and the paper's own Gaussian example shows they need not. It says nothing yet about the information bottleneck beyond a formal transfer through the KL distortion. | Active |
| [THEORY-753](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-753.md) | For finite X and Y, the information bottleneck is successively refinable from budget λ₁ to λ₂ > λ₁ iff some pair of optimal encoders forms a Markov chain X → T₂ → T₁, that is, iff the coarse optimal encoder is a garbling of a fine one; when the fine optimum's decoder points q(X\|t₂) are affinely independent, this holds for that pair iff every decoder point q(X\|t₁) of the coarse optimum lies in their convex hull, so a failed hull test on optima that are unique up to merging and relabelling proves that refinement fails | Charvin, Catenacci Volpi and Polani (2023), [LIT-1258](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1258.md), read in [NOTE-981](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-981.md). It turns [QUESTION-220](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-220.md)'s Markov formulation into a finite check: nesting between two IB optima is a convex-hull inclusion of their decoder points, which a linear programme decides. The check is on given optima, and refinability asks for some pair. So a failed check settles the question only when the optima are certified globally optimal and unique. This entry adds that the information bottleneck's own convex-envelope dual can supply that certificate. Finite alphabets, two stages. | Active |
| [THEORY-756](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-756.md) | The growth rate of thermodynamic depth is the entropy rate of whichever macrostate process it is computed over, so the choice of macrostates sets it anywhere from zero up; among partitions of a stationary process's past that predict every finite stretch of the future as well as the whole past does, the causal states are the coarsest, so they have the least entropy and the least entropy rate | Crutchfield and Shalizi (1999; arXiv 1998), [LIT-1260](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1260.md), read in [NOTE-978](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-978.md). Depth is not a structure measure until its states are fixed. Predictive sufficiency, then minimality, fixes them as the causal states. The choice is canonical only given the measuring instrument and the target, the observed future. The redefined dive is still an entropy rate. | Active |
| [THEORY-757](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-757.md) | The information bottleneck is successively refinable between every pair of budgets when Y is a function of X, by nested erasures of Y, and when X and Y are both binary, where the optimum at each nonzero budget is unique up to merging and relabelling and its two decoder points are the ends of an interval of the source simplex that only widens as the budget grows | Charvin, Catenacci Volpi and Polani (2023), [LIT-1258](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1258.md), read in [NOTE-981](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-981.md). These are the two finite cases in which nested information-bottleneck optima are guaranteed at every pair of budgets. Neither reaches the record's four-state source, whose Y is not a function of X and whose X has three effective states. [NOTE-981](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-981.md) finds that source not refinable. So binary Y alone does not guarantee nesting. The function case is the degenerate one, where the bottleneck is just a noisy copy of Y. | Active |
| [THEORY-764](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-764.md) | For a deterministic supervenient feature V of a Markov system, Rosas et al.'s practical emergence criterion Ψ equals the parts' whole-minus-sum information about V's next value minus V's one-step dynamical dependence I(V_t′; X_t \| V_t), so dynamical independence raises Ψ but neither implies emergence nor is implied by it, and the paper's sufficient test for causal decoupling can pass a feature that is not dynamically independent | Rosas et al. (2020), [LIT-1244](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1244.md), read in [NOTE-987](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-987.md), with Barnett and Seth's dynamical independence ([LIT-979](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-979.md), [THEORY-257](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-257.md)). By the chain rule, Ψ(V) = [I(X_t;V_t′) − Σ_j I(Xʲ_t;V_t′)] − I(V_t′;X_t\|V_t). The subtracted term vanishing implies Barnett–Seth independence for Markov X. Examples show each condition without the other. The independent sum of AR(1) channels has both, with no interaction. The identity concerns Ψ, the paper's practical criterion; it says nothing about the PID quantities themselves. | Active |
| [THEORY-784](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-784.md) | Language models trained on limited data show a test loss falling as P^(−γ/(2β)) because P training tokens resolve token correlations only out to a horizon growing as P^(1/(2β)), so that more data mainly lengthens the context a model can use, when the model learns within that horizon faster than it grows, as Cagnetta, Raventós, Ganguli and Wyart propose | Cagnetta, Raventós, Ganguli and Wyart (2026), [LIT-888](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-888.md), read in [NOTE-689](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-689.md), building on Cagnetta and Wyart's effective context window ([LIT-883](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-883.md)). The paper presents the horizon as the reason the data-limited exponent is γ/(2β). [THEORY-204](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-204.md) holds what it showed: the derivation under assumed scaling forms, and the measured overlap on TinyStories and WikiText-103 up to about 10^8 tokens. Whether the horizon is why is the test [QUESTION-233](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-233.md) asks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-787](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-787.md) v2 | A system's causal structure can be most effective at a macro scale, so that causation emerges at a coarse-grained level and the macro description is the one at which the system's causes are found, as Hoel, Albantakis and Tononi propose from effective information | Hoel, Albantakis and Tononi (2013), [LIT-1038](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1038.md), argue that macro can beat micro: the scale at which effective information peaks is where a system's causal structure is, so causation can emerge at a macro level. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-222](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-222.md), only the arithmetic: under uniform interventions imposed separately at each level, a macro description can have more effective information. This is the causal thesis, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Rejected — Rejected on 2026-10-30, at the owner's direction, by its own refutation condition: the macro advantage disappears whenever the same intervention distribution over micro states is used at both levels. THEORY-1167 proves this for a coarse-graining of one transition, by data processing, and Comolatti and Hoel concede it (LIT-1843). The independent interventionist test the promote_when asks for, causal feature learning (LIT-1833), can confirm that a macro is proportionate but never that it beats the micro (THEORY-1169). What the record holds instead is CLAIM-497, by ARG-041. Hoel's temporal and spatio-temporal macros, which the bound does not reach, are QUESTION-335. The arithmetic it rested on, THEORY-222, stands. |
| [THEORY-788](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-788.md) | Training a deep classifier past zero training error generally collapses its last-layer features onto their class means, drives the centred means toward a simplex equiangular tight frame aligned with the classifier, and makes the decision nearest class mean, as Papyan, Han and Donoho propose from their runs | Papyan, Han and Donoho (2020), [LIT-618](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-618.md), title their paper on the "prevalence" of neural collapse and present it as a pervasive outcome of the terminal phase of training. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-083](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-083.md), only what their runs measured: three architectures with cross-entropy on seven balanced datasets without augmentation. This is the general law, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-789](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-789.md) | The block coarse-graining that maximizes mutual information with the system beyond a buffer picks out the renormalization-group-relevant variables in general, so those variables can be found from samples by information alone, without being known beforehand, as Koch-Janusz and Ringel propose | Koch-Janusz and Ringel (2017), [LIT-873](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-873.md), propose that their mutual-information criterion finds a system's relevant degrees of freedom with no prior knowledge of them. What the record holds as shown, [THEORY-194](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-194.md), is that it recovered variables renormalization already uses, on 2D models whose answer was known. This is the general thesis that result was offered for, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-791](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-791.md) | The colour-naming systems of the world's languages lie near the information-bottleneck bound for compressing perceptual meanings into words, and differences in one trade-off parameter place each language along it, as Zaslavsky, Kemp, Regier and Tishby propose | Zaslavsky, Kemp, Regier & Tishby (2018), [LIT-810](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-810.md), read in [NOTE-631](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-631.md), using the bound of [LIT-338](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-338.md). Their fit covers the World Color Survey languages and English, with the need distribution over meanings estimated from the same naming data, and that measured part is the Active [THEORY-163](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-163.md). The authors present the result as a property of the world's languages. This THEORY holds that general claim. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-804](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-804.md) | Ince's common change in surprisal is a correct measure of the redundancy among any number of sources, and the negative partial-information atoms it gives are local misinformation and mechanistic redundancy, not defects of the measure | The thesis [THEORY-714](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-714.md)'s title carried before the promotion audit (batch 056) corrected and narrowed it to what I_ccs is and which properties it has. Ince (2017), [LIT-1201](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1201.md), proposes I_ccs as the redundancy measure and reads its negative atoms as misinformation and mechanistic redundancy. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. The re-derivation found that I_ccs fails subset equality, the property Ince argues licenses the lattice, which counts against the thesis without settling it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-806](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-806.md) | Translation without parallel data, as of an unknown animal communication system into a human language, is learnable from a plausibility prior over the target language alone, with error falling as the common ground between the languages grows and as the source language grows richer | The general reading that [THEORY-270](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-270.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the common-nonsense model its bound is proved in (batch 044). Goldwasser, Gruber, Kalai and Paradise (NeurIPS 2023), [LIT-941](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-941.md), read in [NOTE-804](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-804.md), motivate their framework by translating animal communication and state its lesson for translation in general, while saying their stylised models are not intended to capture natural language. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-809](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-809.md) | Language models trained by gradient descent on a mixture of random facts and other data reach the capacity-optimal allocation, so the model size and the mixing ratio at which they begin to learn the facts are those of an optimal capacity-bounded learner | The link that [THEORY-293](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-293.md)'s title asserted before the promotion audit narrowed it (batch 036) to the optimal learner's theorem and the observation of a threshold in Pythia models. Gu, Lyu, Li and Zhang (2025), [LIT-984](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-984.md), read in [NOTE-796](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-796.md), explain the trained models' thresholds by the optimal learner's. The one quantitative check, a size exponent of 1.152 against a predicted 1.283, is recorded against it. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-811](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-811.md) | With a kernel normalised to unit diagonal, the kernel quantum relative entropy of two distributions is within O(σ²) of their Kullback–Leibler divergence as the bandwidth σ shrinks, for translation-invariant kernels on the torus generally and for kernels on other compact groups | The general reading that [THEORY-313](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-313.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the one kernel family on the torus that the rate is shown for. Bach (2022), [LIT-255](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-255.md), read in [NOTE-837](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-837.md), asserts that other translation-invariant kernels and kernels on compact groups behave alike, and sketches a leverage-score argument without completing it. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-817](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-817.md) | Once an agent's actions affect the percepts it receives, maximal prediction of those percepts is generally not what thermodynamic efficiency requires: in percept-action loops with feedback, maximally predictive agents generally extract less work than the most efficient agent | Fiderer et al. (2025), [LIT-041](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-041.md), read in [NOTE-032](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-032.md), prove that without feedback the work-efficient agents are exactly the maximally predictive ones that randomise and forget their actions, and that with feedback one binary memoryless channel separates predictive, max-entropy-action and efficient agents; from that they assert that with feedback maximally predictive agents are generally inefficient. The record holds as proved, in [THEORY-026](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-026.md), only the one channel. It does not say that efficiency under feedback is a trade-off between prediction and forgetting: in the proved example the efficient agent is memoryless. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-820](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-820.md) v2 | For a stationary discrete-valued process X and any coarse-graining Z of its past, informational closure at every horizon is the same condition as zero one-step transfer entropy from the micro past, Barnett and Seth's dynamical independence, and as causal closure, Z's ε-machine coinciding with its υ-machine; for a coarse-graining of the present state it also makes Z's causal states a coarse-graining of X's, which does not imply closure, and the closed coarse-grainings are not closed under common refinement | Rosas et al. (arXiv 2024), [LIT-1306](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1306.md), read in [NOTE-1030](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1030.md), with Barnett and Seth's definition ([LIT-979](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-979.md)). For discrete stationary processes, the information-theoretic criterion of emergent closure (dynamical independence), the interventionist one (the macro's own causal states are all the micro distinctions that matter for it) and, for maps of the present state, a computational one are nested as stated. The first two are one condition. It says nothing about approximate closure. It does not make closure a mark of unity. "Causal" is only in the Granger sense unless X is fully observed. | Active |
| [THEORY-822](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-822.md) | For a Markov chain and a partition of its states, strong lumpability, every state of a block sending the same probability into each block, is the column-equitability of the master-equation operator and makes the block label informationally closed; when the chain is irreducible, an informationally closed label that is itself Markov is strongly lumpable, with no aperiodicity needed; weak lumpability gives a Markov label that need not be closed; and the same holds on the causal-state chain of any stationary process | Rosas et al. (arXiv 2024), [LIT-1306](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1306.md), read in [NOTE-1030](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1030.md), on Kemeny–Snell lumpability, joined to Shpak et al.'s column-equitable partitions ([LIT-1242](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1242.md), [THEORY-755](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-755.md)). Exact closure of a block label in a Markov chain is a condition on transition rows, a symmetry, and not weak coupling. The converse needs the label to be Markov: a closed label can have memory. Exact results only, with no bound for nearly lumpable partitions. | Active |
| [THEORY-840](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-840.md) | When every log-likelihood a predictive family V can assign lies in [−B, B], the V-information estimated from N samples is within 4R_N(G_V) + 2B√(2 log(1/δ)/N) of the true V-information with probability at least 1 − 2δ, with R_N(G_V) the Rademacher complexity of the family's log-likelihoods; so usable information relative to a family of small complexity can be estimated in high dimension, and what is estimated is that family's information, not Shannon's | Xu, Zhao, Song, Stewart and Ermon (2020), [LIT-1309](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1309.md), read in [NOTE-1048](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1048.md), Theorem 1. Restricting the predictor class trades the data-processing inequality for estimability. The bound needs bounded log-likelihoods and says nothing about Shannon information, which a restricted family may under- or over-state ([THEORY-846](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-846.md)). | Active |
| [THEORY-844](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-844.md) | A designer who commits to how players are informed, and may condition on the state and on their prior information but cannot choose their actions, can bring about exactly the Bayes correlated equilibria, the joint distributions of states and actions in which no player told his recommended action wants to deviate, a polytope cut out by linear constraints; with one uninformed receiver who would lose 1 by investing in the bad state and gain x < 1 in the good, the most investment attainable is certain investment in the good state and investment with probability x in the bad | Bergemann and Morris (2019), [LIT-1313](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1313.md), read in [NOTE-1034](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1034.md), from the accepted manuscript. What control over information alone can achieve, among Bayesian players with a common prior, is a set computable by linear programming, whoever the designer is, and read metaphorically it bounds what any information structure could produce. It assumes commitment, a designer who picks the equilibrium, and Bayesian players; it says nothing about bounded receivers. | Active |
| [THEORY-846](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-846.md) | Information usable by a predictor restricted to a family V can be created by computing on the data, so the data-processing inequality fails for V-information: with Z the exclusive-or of two fair independent bits, linear and one-coordinate families extract nothing about Z from the pair and all of it from their exclusive-or; V-information computed from any function of the source is bounded by the source's Shannon information when the family's input-free predictions can match the marginal of the target, and can exceed it otherwise | Xu, Zhao, Song, Stewart and Ermon (2020), [LIT-1309](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1309.md), read in [NOTE-1048](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1048.md), define V-information and say it "can be created through computation". The record's worked case is [CLAIM-199](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-199.md)'s XOR under the paper's linear families, and its addition is the ceiling: usable information never exceeds the source's Shannon information when V can predict the marginal of Y without input, and can exceed it when V cannot. It says nothing about which family a real observer has. | Active |
| [THEORY-853](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-853.md) | Giving players more information shrinks what an information designer can make them do: for one player, being more informative in Blackwell's sense, being a garbling's source and leaving a smaller set of Bayes correlated equilibria in every decision problem are the same order; for many players the incentive order is individual sufficiency, which neither implies nor is implied by sufficiency of the players' joint information | Bergemann and Morris (2019), [LIT-1313](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1313.md), read in [NOTE-1034](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1034.md), §4.2. A third face of Blackwell's order: the better-informed receiver is the harder one to steer. For many players the right order is not the statistical sufficiency of their joint information. Bayesian players only; for bounded ones a garbling can make a receiver easier to steer and easier to inform at once. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-881](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-881.md) | Across humans, macaques, marmosets and mice, loss of behavioural responsiveness under anaesthesia goes with lower whole-brain pairwise integrated information ΦR in resting fMRI, and its return goes with ΦR's return, including when central thalamic stimulation restores responsiveness during continued anaesthesia; ΦR tracks the macaque arousal score better than the original Φ, causal density, net information flow or functional connectivity | Luppi et al. (2026), [LIT-1357](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1357.md), read in full in [NOTE-1064](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1064.md) from the open-access version of record. It extends the same group's 2024 result ([LIT-949](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-949.md), [THEORY-240](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-240.md)) from human propofol and disorders of consciousness to four species and six regimes, and adds a causal reversal in two macaques. The sharp edge: the state measured is responsiveness, which the authors call "presumably consciousness" and grant is "an imperfect marker of unconsciousness"; the measure is pairwise, linear-Gaussian and content-free; and one mouse regimen fails the main analysis. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-884](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-884.md) v2 | A retained state supports exact answers to a declared family of questions after every finite sequence of a declared family of total deterministic revisions exactly when each of its fibres lies within one class of the coarsest revision-invariant refinement of agreement on current answers; that refinement can be strictly finer than what present answers require, and at most K* − K revision sequences, beyond the current answers, are needed to tell its K* classes apart | Aevyra (2026), The Ledger of Will, [LIT-1376](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1376.md), read in full in [NOTE-1091](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1091.md): Proposition 4, "revision closure", with its proof in §4.4 and finite checks in Appendix A.9. The authors call it "a finite-machine refinement construction in the tradition of Moore and Nerode", not a new theorem. It answers [QUESTION-112](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-112.md) in one case only: a finite family of total deterministic revisions declared in advance. It does not say how to choose the family, which is that question's hard part, and it is not an efficient construction. | Active |
| [THEORY-1025](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1025.md) | The inputs causal scrubbing samples for a treeified hypothesis are the unique maximum-entropy distribution, on finite inputs, among those that give the inputs of every interpretation node the joint distribution they have on the data, so whatever the hypothesis does not claim is resampled as independently as the claims allow | Chan, Garriga-Alonso, Goldowsky-Dill, Greenblatt et al. (2022), [LIT-1583](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1583.md), read in [NOTE-1202](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1202.md), §5. Every node's datum is distributed as D, so each node's scrubbed inputs are jointly as on the data, and among all distributions with that property the algorithm's has the greatest entropy. It characterizes the sampling, not the score: it does not say that a hypothesis whose score matches the model is true, and the same appendix's §7 builds one that is false. | Active |
| [THEORY-1053](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1053.md) | Under unitary evolution, two states of a quantum system can each leave a record in another system while themselves staying undisturbed only if they are orthogonal or the record does not distinguish them; so the outcomes that can be recorded repeatably form an orthogonal set, a result that uses only unitarity and repeatability and not the Born rule | Zurek (2009), [LIT-1640](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1640.md), eq. (5), read in [NOTE-1229](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1229.md). From \|u⟩\|e₀⟩ → \|u⟩\|e_u⟩ and \|v⟩\|e₀⟩ → \|v⟩\|e_v⟩, preservation of the scalar product gives ⟨u\|v⟩ = ⟨u\|v⟩⟨e_u\|e_v⟩, so either the record is no record or ⟨u\|v⟩ = 0. Zurek reads this as the origin of the outcome set of the collapse postulate. It does not give single outcomes, probabilities or which orthogonal set is chosen; that is the interaction's. | Active |
| [THEORY-1055](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1055.md) | In models of decoherence, the information a small fraction of the environment holds about a system rises steeply to a plateau at the system's entropy H_S, so many disjoint fragments each carry nearly all of it, and this redundancy is high only for the pointer observable; Zurek identifies it with objective existence, many observers learning the pointer state independently and without disturbing the system, though the paper argues and does not prove that a plateau in mutual information gives each observer the same record | Zurek (2009), [LIT-1640](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1640.md), section II and Figs. 2–3, read in [NOTE-1229](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1229.md). Redundancy R_δ = 1/f_δ, the number of disjoint fragments each holding (1 − δ)H_S of the information about S, is large for states made by decoherence and absent for random states, and peaks sharply at the pointer observable. Those are model results the review cites. The step from redundancy to objectivity ("Large redundancy implies objectivity") is an identification. The later caveat, that mutual information alone does not guarantee independently accessible records, is not in the paper. Proposed for that step. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1056](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1056.md) | In angular synchronization with outlier offsets, a polynomial-time spectral relaxation, the top eigenvector of the Hermitian matrix of measured phase offsets, recovers the angles once the share of good offsets exceeds about 1/√n on the complete graph, within a factor √((L − 1)/(2 log₂ L)) of the information bound that limits every algorithm, while exact maximum likelihood is a non-convex search costing O(mLⁿ) exhaustively; in this model the price of recovering the global configuration cheaply instead of optimally is a constant factor in evidence, which vanishes for L ≤ 6 | Singer (2011), [LIT-1655](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1655.md), §§2, 4 and 5, read in [NOTE-1224](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1224.md) from arXiv v2. The threshold p > 1/√n comes from a cited rank-one deformation theorem adopted to a non-Gaussian mixture and a heuristic comparison with random correlation, confirmed by simulation at n = 100 and 400; the near-optimality ratio compares it with an information bound for a different success criterion. Proposed for both steps. It does not say that recovery is cheap on every graph, under every noise model, or for fine angular resolution. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1058](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1058.md) | Given constructor theory's principles of locality and of classical information, a single further prohibition, that two information observables with mutually disjoint attributes have a union that is not an information observable, is enough for a medium to have information attributes that cannot be distinguished, unclonable and jointly unsharp observables, measurements that are deterministic yet unpredictable, irreducible disturbance by measurement, and locally inaccessible information; quantum information is an instance | Deutsch & Marletto (2015), [LIT-1663](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1663.md), §§7–8, read in [NOTE-1219](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1219.md). Active as a conditional. The derivations are informal but complete arguments from principles II–IX, and each feature is shown in the paper's own terms with no probabilities. The principles themselves are conjectures. It does not say that superinformation singles out quantum theory, or that the quantum features are derived from anything not already assumed. | Active |
| [THEORY-1060](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1060.md) | Robinson's claim that sheaves are the canonical data structure for sensor integration rests on an axiomatization, not a theorem: six axioms are posited as what an integrated sensor system must be and a sheaf is defined as whatever satisfies them, the paper calls sheaves one of many co-universal information representations, and its consistency and fusion tools need only a presheaf | Robinson (2017), [LIT-1658](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1658.md), read in [NOTE-1221](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1221.md) from arXiv v3. A textual finding about the paper, Active as such. The word "canonical" is never defined for sheaves as a sensor model; its technical uses are the standard ones for cohomology. It does not say that sheaves are a poor model, or that no theorem of this kind could be proved. | Active |
| [THEORY-1066](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1066.md) | In constructor theory, a set of attributes is an information variable when every permutation of it and its cloning are possible tasks, and distinguishability is defined afterwards, as the possibility of mapping a variable onto an information variable; so information is fixed by counterfactual properties of a substrate without presupposing distinguishability, and instantiating it is stated as an intrinsic property of the substrate in the sense of referring to no other specific substrate | Deutsch & Marletto (2015), [LIT-1663](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1663.md), §§3–5, read in [NOTE-1219](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1219.md). Active as a fact about the construction: the definitions are given in that order, and the base they give the recursion of (1.1) is checkable on the page. It does not say that these notions are the intuitive ones, which the authors disclaim, nor that the principles built on them hold. Its "intrinsic" excludes reference to a specific other substrate, not to generic ones, which the cloning task and (5.1) both use. | Active |
| [THEORY-1067](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1067.md) | In angular synchronization from m pairwise offsets, each exact with probability p and otherwise uniform over L values, no estimator of any computational cost can recover all n angles with small error when p is below about √((n/m)·2 log₂ L/(L − 1)), nor an angle of average degree below about √((n/m)·log₂ L/(L − 1)), because each offset carries at most I(L, p) ≈ ½(L − 1)p² bits; below these thresholds a global configuration that exists is not determined by the pairwise evidence, whatever the resources spent on finding it | Singer (2011), [LIT-1655](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1655.md), §5, read in [NOTE-1224](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1224.md) from arXiv v2. Active as mathematics: Fano's inequality applied to an explicit entropy count, asymptotic in m, n → ∞, p → 0 with L fixed. The bound is loose (it ignores the dependencies among offsets) and covers exact recovery and per-angle recovery, not partial correlation, which the eigenvector method achieves below it. It says nothing of what a bounded algorithm can do above it. | Active |
| [THEORY-1069](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1069.md) | In a von Neumann measurement the measuring variable's information about the measured variable grows continuously under the unitary coupling, in Di Biagio and Rovelli's model as I_{A:B}(t) = sin²(ωt)H_A, so the discontinuity of a quantum measurement lies only in a threshold on when information counts as a fact; with an idealized pure ready state a fact conditional on a pointer value appears at once, which they attribute to the idealization | Di Biagio and Rovelli (2025), [LIT-1676](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1676.md), read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1214](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1214.md), §VII and App. B. Active as mathematics: (B7) follows from (B6), which I rederived; (B8) as printed has a sign error, and the correct form is I_A^max − cos²(ωt)H_A. The continuity is of the expected quantities. A conditional relative fact appears at once in the ideal model, and the full-rank case that would remove that is described, not computed. The authors say the point is not specifically quantum. | Active |
| [THEORY-1077](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1077.md) | On a presheaf of pseudometric spaces, the consistency radius of an assignment, the largest distance between an observation and the restriction of another, is zero exactly for assignments induced by global sections (in metric spaces) and, when the restrictions are K-Lipschitz, bounds the assignment's sup-distance from every global section below by ε/(1 + K); so fusing data into a consistent state must move it at least that far, and the bound needs no sheaf condition | Robinson (2017), [LIT-1658](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1658.md), Definition 20 and Propositions 21 and 23, read in [NOTE-1221](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1221.md) from arXiv v3; both proofs checked. Active as mathematics. It does not say that the nearest global section is unique (the paper's Proposition 25 claims so for Banach sheaves and the proof does not reach it), that the radius locates a fault, or that a small radius means the data are right. | Active |
| [THEORY-1092](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1092.md) | Read over the sensor domains, the discrepancies between each observation and the restrictions of others can single out a faulty sensor where the consistency radius alone does not: in Robinson's simulated search, a 2° bearing bias was attributed to the right sensor, without prior knowledge of it, because every large discrepancy involved that sensor's domains, while the radius was lower than in the unbiased case | Robinson (2017), [LIT-1658](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1658.md), Example 24, Case 2 (pp. 26–28 of arXiv v3), read in [NOTE-1221](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1221.md). One simulated case, one noise realization, read from a figure. Proposed until a stated procedure is tested over trials, including faults in the restriction maps, which enter the discrepancies in the same way as faults in the data. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1093](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1093.md) | In Di Biagio and Rovelli's reformulation of relational quantum mechanics a relative fact is a conditional probability concentrated on one value: A is a fact relative to B when the relative information I_{A\|B} = I_A + I_{A:B} is maximal; since only commuting variables have a joint distribution, perspectives belong to commutative subalgebras of observables, not to quantum systems, so a qubit has none, and the joint distribution is itself relative to a further system, so the relativity iterates | Di Biagio and Rovelli (2025), [LIT-1676](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1676.md), read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1214](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1214.md), §§II–V and IX. Active as a statement of the paper's definitions and of what follows from them: eq. (7) is an identity, and the restriction to commuting variables follows from the existence of joint distributions. It does not say that this resolves the problems the authors list, that observers play no role in fixing what counts as a fact, or that the choice of subalgebra is given by the physics. | Active |
| [THEORY-1096](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1096.md) | Blackwell's comparison of experiments, its easy direction: an experiment is a family of distributions indexed by a common parameter, and if one experiment is a garbling of another by a Markov kernel, every risk attainable with the garbling in any decision problem with bounded losses is attainable with the original, on any outcome spaces | Split from [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md) by the status review of 2026-10-27 ([ADR-057](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md)). [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md)'s equivalence needs a second proof of the general converse and stays Proposed. Ten of its twelve dependents used only its definitions (an experiment, a garbling, the informativeness order), or only the easy direction, that a garbling never helps a decision-maker free to choose any rule. The easy direction holds on any outcome spaces, and its proof is two lines, re-derived below under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v2's ruling, which [ADR-057](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md) keeps. It is Theorem 3 of Blackwell (1953), [LIT-781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-781.md), read in [NOTE-595](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-595.md), and Blackwell's 1951 result. The finite converse is [THEORY-717](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-717.md), Active. | Active |
| [THEORY-1125](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1125.md) | For discrete X and Y, with an intervention on a variable abstraction T of X defined as the mixture of interventions on X weighted by Bayes inversion of the encoder under a protocol prior, no abstraction gains causal information about Y over X itself, and at full weight on causal control the causal information bottleneck is optimised by the partition of X by p(y \| do(x)), mapped one class to one value of T, uniquely up to relabelling when T has exactly as many values as there are classes; these are Chalupka et al.'s causal macrovariables | Simoes, Dastani and van Ommen (UAI 2025), [LIT-1802](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1802.md), Proposition 20 with its proof (pp. 14–15), read in [NOTE-1347](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1347.md) from the arXiv preprint v5. Active: the proof is a strict-concavity argument, checked here on the paper's Genetic Mutations SCM. It is the interventional counterpart of [THEORY-743](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-743.md), and unlike the bottleneck there it reaches the partition exactly, because γ = 1 drops the compression term. It holds for the paper's stipulated intervention on T and a fixed protocol; it says nothing about intermediate γ. | Active |
| [THEORY-1127](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1127.md) | A CycleGAN trained to translate aerial photographs to maps and back satisfies its cycle-consistency loss by encoding details of the photograph in a low-amplitude, high-frequency signal in the generated map: the reconstruction recovers details the visible map lacks, is destroyed by noise of three 8-bit levels or by JPEG compression and survives low-frequency change, and the same sensitivity lets an imperceptible perturbation of almost any map make the reverse generator output any chosen photograph | Chu, Zhmoginov and Sandler (2017), [LIT-1800](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1800.md), §§2–4, read in [NOTE-1346](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1346.md). One trained model on one dataset. The noise curve (Fig. 3, 50 photographs) is the only quantitative result; the hidden details, the composing edits and the attack are shown by examples. Proposed: an empirical finding about one model, said by the authors to recur on other datasets, not shown. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1143](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1143.md) | When one domain carries more information than the other, a translation trained only to make the round trip close cannot meet that requirement through a correspondence in the intermediate's visible code, so the round trip closes through a channel the intermediate's audience does not read; agreement of the round trip with its source therefore says nothing about whether the intermediate renders the source's content for that audience | Chu, Zhmoginov and Sandler (2017), [LIT-1800](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1800.md), §2 and §5, read in [NOTE-1346](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1346.md). The authors argue it from the many photographs a single map stands for, and support it with [THEORY-1127](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1127.md)'s evidence on one model; they propose, and do not run, the test of adding capacity to the smaller domain. Proposed. It is the converse of the record's collapse case for [CLAIM-496](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-496.md): there routes agree because nothing travels, here because everything does, out of sight. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1146](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1146.md) v2 | Under confounding the partition of a variable X by what it predicts about a target Y can differ from its partition by what setting it does to Y, so the information bottleneck at full sufficiency can learn distinctions no intervention could use and miss ones only intervention reveals, as it did in two confounded toy models, while the causal information bottleneck, computed from observational data through a backdoor set, recovered the causal partition in all three toy models, projected gradient search finding it in 95 to 100 percent of runs | Simoes, Dastani and van Ommen (UAI 2025), [LIT-1802](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1802.md), §8 and Appendices E–F, read in [NOTE-1347](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1347.md). Three SCMs with 7, 4 and 16 values of X; ensembles of 4 to 12 optimisers; a penalty against unused values of T was needed at full control. The difference between the partitions follows from the definitions; what the experiments add is that the search finds the causal one, in toy problems only. Active as a report (ADR-065); whether search finds it at scale is QUESTION-346. | Active |
| [THEORY-1163](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1163.md) | Krakauer et al.'s organismal and colonial individuality, A* = I(S_{n+1}; S_n) and A = I(S_{n+1}; S_n \| E_n), cannot decrease when variables are moved from the environment into the candidate system, so maximizing either over candidate boundaries selects the largest candidate, and a boundary found this way needs a size cost the measures do not contain | Krakauer, Bertschinger, Olbrich, Flack and Ay (2020), [LIT-1137](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1137.md), read in [NOTE-1400](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1400.md). Mutual information cannot fall when either argument is enlarged, and A′ ≥ A follows by the chain rule with the remaining environment as condition. It is a fact about the measures, not about any system. It does not say how to price size, and nC, the third measure, can move either way. It is the formal content of A11's remark recorded in [QUESTION-115](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-115.md). | Active |
