| [THEORY-1167](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1167.md) v2 | When one intervention distribution over micro states is used at both levels, the effective information of a coarse-graining of a discrete mechanism, with each macro intervention realized by that distribution within its block, cannot exceed the micro effective information; so a positive causal emergence of effective information, scored with a uniform distribution at each level, equals the micro gain from changing the distribution minus a non-negative loss, and is a gain from the change of distribution | The test [QUESTION-204](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-204.md) asks for has an answer that needs no system: with one distribution over micro states at both levels, EI(macro) = I(f(X); f(Y)) ≤ I(X; Y) = EI(micro) by data processing. Hoel's causal emergence uses the uniform distribution at each level, which is a non-uniform micro distribution whenever blocks differ in size, so its positive values come from the micro chain scored under that other distribution. Comolatti and Hoel ([LIT-1843](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1843.md)) concede the stationary case; Eberhardt and Lee ([LIT-1839](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1839.md)) name the distribution as the source of the artefact. It says nothing about measures that data processing does not bound, nor about whether EI's level agrees with an interventionist test. | Active |
| [THEORY-1169](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1169.md) | For a discrete mechanism scored with one full-support intervention distribution over micro causes at both levels, a coarse-graining of cause and effect keeps all of the micro effective information if and only if it merges only causes with identical rows P(Y \| do(x)) and only effects with proportional columns, whatever the distribution; so the coarsest coarse-graining that ties the micro is the causal partition of causal feature learning, with effects grouped by normalized likelihood, and any merge of causes with different effects loses information under every such distribution | Causal feature learning ([LIT-1833](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1833.md), [LIT-1834](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1834.md)) defines macro causes as classes of micro states with the same interventional effect, with no distribution over interventions. Under one full-support distribution w at both levels, the loss of effective information from a coarse-graining (f, g) is I(X; Y \| g(Y)) + I(X; g(Y) \| f(X)), and both terms vanish exactly when f merges only equal rows and g only proportional columns, for every w. So the ties that [THEORY-1167](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1167.md) allows are the causal-feature-learning partitions and their refinements: on which coarse-graining loses nothing, EI under a common distribution and the interventionist test agree, and the agreement is distribution-free. How much a merge loses still depends on w. Hoel's EI, uniform at each level, parts from it on Eberhardt and Lee's (13), (14) and note 6. | Active |
| [THEORY-1177](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1177.md) | For experiments on a finite parameter set, being at least as informative for every decision problem is the same as being able to simulate the other by a randomisation | The wide form [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md) held before the twelfth status review narrowed it, kept as a Proposed reading by the [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind-1 sweep of 2026-10-30: the source asserts it, and [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md), Active, is its evidence. Blackwell (1953), [LIT-781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-781.md), claims the equivalence for any outcome space, through Theorem 2, quoted from his 1951 paper. The record's re-derivation reaches only outcome spaces that are standard Borel, since its last step needs a regular conditional distribution. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1245](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1245.md) | Evaluating expected free energy recursively over the beliefs an agent would hold after each plausible outcome makes active inference a pruned tree search over belief states, formally analogous to Bellman recursion, which lets the agent plan through short-term costs that one-step agents cannot; that the pruning keeps deep search tractable beyond toy problems is argued, not shown | The general form of Friston, Da Costa, Hafner, Hesp and Parr (2020), [LIT-577](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-577.md), under [THEORY-426](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-426.md)'s old title. It was kept here when the twenty-fourth status review narrowed [THEORY-426](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-426.md) to the paper's runs and promoted it ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §3; [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1). The paper shows the planning claim only in single deterministic runs on a T-maze and an 8 × 8 maze ([NOTE-454](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-454.md), C2). It argues tractability from pruning and sparsity and counts evaluations for one maze (C3). It tries no problem where many outcomes stay plausible, and runs no Bayes-adaptive planner beside it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1254](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1254.md) | A controller that must stay safe under every model it has not ruled out cannot use the evidence its committing action produces: if the information it can gather before its first action that forecloses a safe continuation under an alternative is bounded by β, every such controller forfeits at least about ½e^{−β} of the value reachable only by committing, so a linear oracle gap gives linear regret, and acting on an exclusion at risk α needs about log(1/(2α)) nats gathered beforehand | Saligrama (2026), [LIT-1880](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1880.md), Theorem 1 and its examples, read in [NOTE-1466](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1466.md). The proof is data processing on the stopped record plus Bretagnolle–Huber, and the explicit relaxation and one example's optimization were checked numerically. Active: a theorem with a short proof, checked. It is a lower bound only; bounded information is sufficient for an unavoidable gap, and unbounded information does not by itself give recovery. | Active |
| [THEORY-1259](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1259.md) | When a teacher's next-token distribution depends on a context the student cannot observe, the forward-KL-optimal student is the teacher averaged over the contexts compatible with the student's observation, the loss it cannot remove is the conditional mutual information between the teacher's output and the hidden context, and the optimal student is at least as uncertain as the teacher is on average; the self-distillation objectives actually trained may not be forward KL at all | Hossain, Kousar and Tourni (2026), [LIT-1883](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1883.md), Proposition 1; read in [NOTE-1479](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1479.md). Active: elementary and checked numerically. This is the published statement of the limit [QUESTION-361](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-361.md) starts from. It holds for the unclipped forward KL; the OPSD objective the paper trains clips each vocabulary entry, which the paper shows reverses the gradient on the teacher's most preferred tokens. | Active |
